title: Unified handoff adapter: graceful bridge between AsyncIterable and Web Streams for TS SDK
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: consumers of the TypeScript SDK currently choose between two primary streaming interfaces: AsyncIterable (for idiomatic JS/TS loops) and Web Streams (for browser-native pipeline composition). Existing bridging helpers are fragmented, opinionated, or brittle around cancellation, lock semantics, and backpressure. This ticket defines and implements a small, well-documented adapter that provides a stable, ergonomic handoff layer between AsyncIterable and ReadableStream/TransformStream for client responses (unary streaming, chat streaming, and duplex cases).

Goals:
- Provide a single library export that can convert AsyncIterable -> ReadableStream and vice versa with predictable semantics.
- Preserve cancellation semantics (early return from for-await-of cancels upstream request).
- Respect Web Streams locking rules (ensure consumers can pipe / tee / getReader without surprising locking errors).
- Support progressive consumption (first token delivered immediately, KV/prefix caching integration later).
- Provide optional buffering strategies for transient bursts while preserving latency SLOs.
- Ship ergonomic examples and migration guidance for existing users.

Non-goals:
- Reimplement full browser polyfills; rely on built-in Web Streams when available and fall back to lightweight shims only for Node runtimes used by customers.

Design notes and tradeoffs: adapter exposes two primary helpers: toReadableStream(asyncIterable, opts) and toAsyncIterable(readableStream, opts). Implementation must avoid copying the whole response body and should favor incremental transfer with configurable highWaterMark. For AsyncIterable -> ReadableStream, we must create a transformed stream that enqueues chunks as they arrive but defers locking until a consumer explicitly requests it. For ReadableStream -> AsyncIterable, we will implement an async generator wrapper that buffers up to N chunks and yields them in arrival order while preserving cancellation by calling reader.cancel() on early exit. Backpressure will be surfaced via an internal acknowledgement mechanism: when buffer hits highWaterMark, upstream pulls should be paused if running in a bridging runtime that supports it (Node streaming).

Compatibility: The API should play nicely with our TS SDK streaming surface (createStream, chat.stream, etc.) and be exported from the main package under streams.handoff. The helper should work equally in Node 18+ and modern browsers.

Testing: unit tests covering cancellation, double-consume attempts, tee scenarios, and stress tests to surface ordering and memory growth. End-to-end example tests using the hosted API with small streaming responses to validate latency and correctness.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter implemented and exported at streams.handoff in TS SDK
Bidirectional conversions: AsyncIterable -> ReadableStream and ReadableStream -> AsyncIterable pass interop contract tests
Cancellation semantics verified: early return cancels upstream request in both directions
Backpressure honored with configurable buffer config; stress tests demonstrate bounded memory for high concurrency
API docs, code examples (node/browser), and migration guide merged in docs repo
Automated tests and at least two integration examples in examples/ts/streams are green in CI
Performance regression threshold: no more than 5% additional p99 latency on small responses compared to raw AsyncIterable
